Before you go, one thing: back in March you sent a Hammer DC02 back on an RMA. What made you stick with Hammer for this BC04?

The units run fine - Helium is more expensive, but we find the builds to be a lot more higher quality. The D.02 came with a broken screen - but still ran, despite me thinking that returning the whole unit was a wasted cost on your end. Good that we got support though.
That's useful, thanks. Would you rather we had just mailed you a replacement screen and left the unit with you?

Fair point, and noted. We do mail single parts now for exactly that kind of thing, so a cracked screen shouldn't cost anyone a whole box again.

Thanks for taking the time, Graham. Abel will come back to you on the $50, and your BC04 ships within 2 business days.

Nice little lab. Four DC02s on Scrypt plus a BC04 on SHA-256 is a good mix to run side by side.

If you ever want a hand tuning them or comparing what they're actually stacking, just open a chat. Abel will be in touch on the $50.
we're pretty good at that stuff around here as we run a couple of pools, so we have all types of miners kicking around to test out

Then you're well ahead of me on that front.

Worth saying to Abel when he comes in, by the way. Pool operators testing hardware is exactly the kind of thing the team likes to hear about, and JD is always keen on real-world numbers from people running mixed fleets.
JD loaded a screen for me when I met him and Georges a month back when I was in Mtl, so I came back with the new HarloOS ready to plug and play on one of the DC02s

That's JD all over, sending people home with a flashed screen.

One thing worth doing before you compare notes across the fleet: check what version each unit reports and grab the latest build for its model from harlolabs.com. Running them all on the same release makes the numbers mean something. The Harlo OS channel on our Discord is the fastest place to get JD on anything odd you see.
